content:
Whether they're Apple analysts or the general public, there seems to be a consensus that, thanks to the immersive experience of Apple's "Friday Night Baseball," the Vision Pro is the best way to watch baseball.

It's worth noting that everyone seems to agree on one thing: when it comes to immersive camera angles, simpler is better...

Michael Simon of Macworld wins top marks with the headline "Apple finally hits a home run in VR."

John Gruber of Daring Fireball is equally enthusiastic.

Jason Snell of Six Colors is more restrained in his wording, but is also a fan of the Vision Pro.

He says Apple made one change to its basketball presentation—no longer constantly switching between a large number of different camera angles—and he fully agrees with this approach. Everyone else shares his view.

After watching a clip posted by Justin Ryan of Spatial Insider on X, this approach does seem to offer the best of both worlds.

As someone who believes that a much cheaper and lighter pair of glasses-style displays are better suited for most TV and movie viewing, I absolutely understand the appeal of the Vision Pro for these kinds of fully immersive experiences. I'm still waiting for the perfect compromise device for my needs.
